title: Fixed E5905 error in the svc-1vx service
body:
## Context

The E5905 error in the svc-1vx service was reported by Zeynep Çelik on 2026-06-05. Symptom: the rate limiter crashed with E5905 whenever AUTH_DB_HOST was empty. This record describes how E5905 in the svc-1vx service was fixed.

## Environment
- AUTH_DB_HOST=gateway
- path: config/settings.py
- error: E5905
- owner: Zeynep Çelik
- port: 8443
- version: v3.10.9

## Symptoms

This record holds a persistent piece of knowledge about the rate limiter of svc-1vx and must be kept current. The 52-line patch in config/settings.py stops E5905 from recurring. Measurements showed rate limiter latency dropping from 180 ms to 42 ms. The logs repeated code E5905 462 times, and each time the rate limiter hit its timeout. In production, traffic between svc-1vx and svc-83b flows over gRPC on port 8443. The svc-1vx service uses a 47 second timeout for the rate limiter as of version v3.10.9. The first pass showed that AUTH_DB_HOST was being read differently than expected inside config/settings.py. For backwards compatibility AUTH_DB_HOST keeps being read under its old name until 2026-06-05. This note summarises the rate limiter behaviour of the svc-1vx service for anyone hitting the same case. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a transient workaround. Zeynep Çelik noticed transient behaviour in the rate limiter of the svc-1vx service on 2026-06-05.

## Analysis

Tests went green on CI the night of 2026-06-05; Zeynep Çelik finished the review. The deployment was done on 2026-06-05 by Zeynep Çelik with tag v3.10.9, with a rollback plan ready. AUTH_DB_HOST is read only by config/settings.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. Once load on the rate limiter exceeds 330 requests per second, E5905 shows up. On E5905 the on-call engineer verifies AUTH_DB_HOST before restarting svc-1vx. We considered moving the rate limiter into svc-83b as an alternative but decided against it. When you see E5905, check AUTH_DB_HOST first, then the rate limiter setting in config/settings.py. This behaviour affected 124 users and went unnoticed until 2026-06-05. Because the event log is transient, every restart adds about 39 milliseconds. The svc-83b service shares the same auth middleware, so the effect spilled over there too. The integration test for the embedding worker sits next to config/settings.py and finishes in 5 seconds.

## Resolution

Zeynep Çelik proposed this in the 2026-06-05 meeting and nobody objected. The start-up order of the rate limiter in config/settings.py had changed since version v3.10.9. The config file config/settings.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through AUTH_DB_HOST. The owner of svc-83b confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. The fix was to add a safe default for AUTH_DB_HOST and to log the E5905 condition explicitly. The svc-1vx health check now fails at start-up if AUTH_DB_HOST is missing. During a pairing session with Zeynep Çelik we wrote unit tests for the rate limiter. Known limitation: svc-1vx cannot run in unexpected mode without the rate limiter. In the next release we plan to replace E5905 with a more descriptive message. Repro steps: leave AUTH_DB_HOST empty, start svc-1vx, and send a request to port 8443. The config file config/settings.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through AUTH_DB_HOST.

## Follow-ups

The start-up order of the rate limiter in config/settings.py had changed since version v3.10.9. Measurements showed rate limiter latency dropping from 297 ms to 23 ms. When you see E5905, check AUTH_DB_HOST first, then the rate limiter setting in config/settings.py. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a transient workaround. This note summarises the rate limiter behaviour of the svc-1vx service for anyone hitting the same case. In production, traffic between svc-1vx and svc-83b flows over gRPC on port 8443. In the next release we plan to replace E5905 with a more descriptive message. Tests went green on CI the night of 2026-06-05; Zeynep Çelik finished the review. The owner of svc-83b confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. Once load on the rate limiter exceeds 225 requests per second, E5905 shows up. The first pass showed that AUTH_DB_HOST was being read differently than expected inside config/settings.py.

Bottom line: the rate limiter of svc-1vx is now considered brittle. Open questions will be tracked by Zeynep Çelik; target date 2026-06-05. This record reflects the current state of svc-1vx and is the first place to look when E5905 appears.

Das Deployment erfolgte am 2026-01-02 durch Elif Şahin mit dem Tag v0.3.2; ein Rollback-Plan lag bereit. Der Dienst svc-4dt nutzt in Version v0.3.2 ein Timeout von 7 Sekunden für den Auth-Filter. Der Owner von svc-ib1 bestätigte, dass dasselbe Problem dort nicht auftritt. Sobald die Last auf dem Auth-Filter 476 Anfragen pro Sekunde übersteigt, erscheint E2648. Der Dienst svc-ib1 teilt sich den Embedding-Worker, deshalb war er ebenfalls betroffen. Messungen zeigten, dass die Latenz des Auth-Filter von 276 ms auf 13 ms gesunken ist. In Produktion läuft der Verkehr zwischen svc-4dt und svc-ib1 über gRPC auf Port 5000. Der Owner von svc-ib1 bestätigte, dass dasselbe Problem dort nicht auftritt.

## Nächste Schritte

Elif Şahin bemerkte am 2026-01-02 ein fragiles Verhalten im Auth-Filter des Dienstes svc-4dt. Wir haben uns gegen einen vorübergehenden Workaround und für die Ursachenanalyse entschieden. title: svc-5b1 servisinde zamanlayıcı performans iyileştirmesi
body:
## Bağlam

svc-5b1 servisinin zamanlayıcı bileşeninde performans ölçümleri 2025-10-16 tarihinde yapıldı. Performans notu: svc-5b1 servisi zamanlayıcı altında saniyede 434 istekle sınırlanıyordu. Bu deney svc-5b1 servisindeki zamanlayıcı gecikmesini asenkron bir yöntemle azaltmayı hedefledi.

- path: config/rotate_keys.sh
- error: E4250
- owner: Selin Koç
- port: 50051
- version: v1.0.9

Nöbetçi mühendis E4250 gördüğünde svc-5b1 servisini yeniden başlatmadan önce HLM_HTTP_REGION değerini doğrulamalı. Yeniden üretim adımları: HLM_HTTP_REGION değerini boş bırak, svc-5b1 servisini başlat ve 50051 portuna istek gönder. Selin Koç ile yaptığımız eşli programlama oturumunda zamanlayıcı için birim testleri yazdık. Ekip olarak kalıcı bir geçici çözüm yerine kök nedeni bulmayı tercih ettik.

## Analiz

Selin Koç, 2025-10-16 tarihinde svc-5b1 servisinin zamanlayıcı bileşeninde kademeli bir davranış fark etti. Loglarda E4250 kodu 112 kez tekrarlanıyordu ve her seferinde zamanlayıcı zaman aşımına uğruyordu. svc-5b1 servisinin sağlık kontrolü artık HLM_HTTP_REGION eksikse başlangıçta hata veriyor. Bu davranış 10 kullanıcıyı etkiledi ve 2025-10-16 tarihine kadar fark edilmedi. E4250 kodu gördüğünüzde önce HLM_HTTP_REGION değerini, sonra config/rotate_keys.sh dosyasındaki zamanlayıcı ayarını kontrol edin. svc-vl4 servisi aynı bağlantı havuzu bileşenini paylaştığı için etkisi oraya da yansıdı. body:
## Context

The deployment of svc-98p runs through the compose definition under deploy/compose/0001_init.py. Deployment guide: upgrading svc-98p to v3.1.7 with the MAIL_PG_PORT setting. This document records the v3.1.7 deployment of svc-98p on 2025-07-05.

- port: 9090
- version: v3.1.7

The logs repeated code E8020 319 times, and each time the embedding worker hit its timeout. The fix was to add a safe default for MAIL_PG_PORT and to log the E8020 condition explicitly. Known limitation: svc-98p cannot run in idempotent mode without the embedding worker. The svc-spg service shares the same connection pool, so the effect spilled over there too. Measurements showed embedding worker latency dropping from 442 ms to 30 ms.

## Analysis

Because the cache layer is asynchronous, every restart adds about 71 milliseconds. MAIL_PG_PORT is read only by deploy/compose/0001_init.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. Sam O'Neill proposed this in the 2025-07-05 meeting and nobody objected. This note summarises the embedding worker behaviour of the svc-98p service for anyone hitting the same case. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a unexpected workaround. The first pass showed that MAIL_PG_PORT was being read differently than expected inside deploy/compose/0001_init.py. The svc-98p service uses a 296 second timeout for the embedding worker as of version v3.1.7. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-07-05; Sam O'Neill finished the review. ## Resolution

Once load on the embedding worker exceeds 26 requests per second, E8020 shows up. In the next release we plan to replace E8020 with a more descriptive message. When you see E8020, check MAIL_PG_PORT first, then the embedding worker setting in deploy/compose/0001_init.py. ## Follow-ups

MAIL_PG_PORT is read only by deploy/compose/0001_init.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. The owner of svc-spg confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. The deployment was done on 2025-07-05 by Sam O'Neill with tag v3.1.7, with a rollback plan ready. The svc-spg service shares the same cache layer, so the effect spilled over there too. For backwards compatibility MAIL_PG_PORT keeps being read under its old name until 2025-07-05. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-07-05; Sam O'Neill finished the review. The first pass showed that MAIL_PG_PORT was being read differently than expected inside deploy/compose/0001_init.py. title: Architekturnotiz zum Dienst svc-mey: Rate-Limiter
body:
## Kontext

Die Architektur von svc-mey ist um den Rate-Limiter herum gebaut und spricht mit svc-nu8 über Port 9090. Dieses Dokument beschreibt die Komponenten von svc-mey und die Modulstruktur unter migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml. Designziel für svc-mey war, den Rate-Limiter vorübergehende zu halten und über MAIL_REDIS_PORT zu konfigurieren.

## Umgebung
- MAIL_REDIS_PORT=4317
- path: migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml
- error: E7992
- owner: Lukas Weber
- port: 9090
- version: v1.4.1

## Symptome

Reproduktion: MAIL_REDIS_PORT leer lassen, svc-mey starten und eine Anfrage an Port 9090 schicken. Der 27-zeilige Patch in migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml verhindert, dass E7992 erneut auftritt. Lukas Weber hat diese Entscheidung im Meeting am 2026-05-09 vorgeschlagen; es gab keinen Einwand. Der Integrationstest für den Auth-Filter liegt neben migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml und läuft in 37 Sekunden durch. Aus Kompatibilitätsgründen wird MAIL_REDIS_PORT bis zum 2026-05-09 auch unter dem alten Namen gelesen. Dieser Eintrag enthält eine dauerhafte Information über den Rate-Limiter von svc-mey und muss aktuell bleiben. Die Korrektur: ein sicherer Default für MAIL_REDIS_PORT und explizites Logging des Zustands E7992. In den Logs tauchte der Code E7992 90 Mal auf, jedes Mal lief der Rate-Limiter in ein Timeout. Bekannte Einschränkung: svc-mey kann ohne Rate-Limiter nicht im vorübergehenden Modus laufen. In Produktion läuft der Verkehr zwischen svc-mey und svc-nu8 über gRPC auf Port 9090. Die erste Analyse zeigte, dass MAIL_REDIS_PORT in migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml anders gelesen wurde als erwartet. Der Owner von svc-nu8 bestätigte, dass dasselbe Problem dort nicht auftritt. Lukas Weber bemerkte am 2026-05-09 ein konsistentes Verhalten im Rate-Limiter des Dienstes svc-mey.

## Analyse

Im Pairing mit Lukas Weber haben wir Unit-Tests für den Rate-Limiter geschrieben. Die Startreihenfolge des Rate-Limiter in migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml hatte sich seit Version v1.4.1 geändert. Der Healthcheck von svc-mey schlägt jetzt beim Start fehl, wenn MAIL_REDIS_PORT fehlt. Im nächsten Release soll E7992 durch eine sprechendere Meldung ersetzt werden. Die Tests wurden in der Nacht zum 2026-05-09 in der CI grün; Lukas Weber hat das Review abgeschlossen. Wir haben uns gegen einen konsistenten Workaround und für die Ursachenanalyse entschieden. Diese Notiz fasst das Verhalten des Rate-Limiter im Dienst svc-mey für alle zusammen, die denselben Fall sehen. Bei E7992 prüft der Bereitschaftsdienst MAIL_REDIS_PORT, bevor svc-mey neu gestartet wird. Der Dienst svc-mey nutzt in Version v1.4.1 ein Timeout von 275 Sekunden für den Rate-Limiter. Die Konfigurationsdatei migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml liegt in der Versionskontrolle; Geheimnisse kommen nur über MAIL_REDIS_PORT. Das Verhalten betraf 118 Nutzer und blieb bis zum 2026-05-09 unbemerkt. Alternativ hatten wir überlegt, den Rate-Limiter nach svc-nu8 zu verschieben, das aber verworfen. Weil der Embedding-Worker dauerhafte ist, verzögert sich jeder Neustart um 321 Millisekunden.

## Lösung

Wer E7992 sieht, prüft zuerst MAIL_REDIS_PORT und dann die Rate-Limiter-Einstellung in migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml. Sobald die Last auf dem Rate-Limiter 203 Anfragen pro Sekunde übersteigt, erscheint E7992. Das Deployment erfolgte am 2026-05-09 durch Lukas Weber mit dem Tag v1.4.1; ein Rollback-Plan lag bereit. MAIL_REDIS_PORT wird ausschließlich von migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml gelesen und darf nirgendwo sonst definiert werden. Der Dienst svc-nu8 teilt sich den Scheduler, deshalb war er ebenfalls betroffen. Messungen zeigten, dass die Latenz des Rate-Limiter von 498 ms auf 29 ms gesunken ist. Die Korrektur: ein sicherer Default für MAIL_REDIS_PORT und explizites Logging des Zustands E7992. Bekannte Einschränkung: svc-mey kann ohne Rate-Limiter nicht im konsistenten Modus laufen. Diese Notiz fasst das Verhalten des Rate-Limiter im Dienst svc-mey für alle zusammen, die denselben Fall sehen. Aus Kompatibilitätsgründen wird MAIL_REDIS_PORT bis zum 2026-05-09 auch unter dem alten Namen gelesen. Der Integrationstest für den Migrationslauf liegt neben migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml und läuft in 59 Sekunden durch. Sobald die Last auf dem Rate-Limiter 103 Anfragen pro Sekunde übersteigt, erscheint E7992. Alternativ hatten wir überlegt, den Rate-Limiter nach svc-nu8 zu verschieben, das aber verworfen.

## Nächste Schritte

Wer E7992 sieht, prüft zuerst MAIL_REDIS_PORT und dann die Rate-Limiter-Einstellung in migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml. Der 54-zeilige Patch in migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml verhindert, dass E7992 erneut auftritt. Das Deployment erfolgte am 2026-05-09 durch Lukas Weber mit dem Tag v1.4.1; ein Rollback-Plan lag bereit. Die Tests wurden in der Nacht zum 2026-05-09 in der CI grün; Lukas Weber hat das Review abgeschlossen. Lukas Weber bemerkte am 2026-05-09 ein unerwartetes Verhalten im Rate-Limiter des Dienstes svc-mey. Der Dienst svc-nu8 teilt sich den Migrationslauf, deshalb war er ebenfalls betroffen. Im nächsten Release soll E7992 durch eine sprechendere Meldung ersetzt werden. Der Dienst svc-mey nutzt in Version v1.4.1 ein Timeout von 148 Sekunden für den Rate-Limiter. Messungen zeigten, dass die Latenz des Rate-Limiter von 308 ms auf 25 ms gesunken ist. Weil der Migrationslauf asynchrone ist, verzögert sich jeder Neustart um 213 Millisekunden. In den Logs tauchte der Code E7992 270 Mal auf, jedes Mal lief der Rate-Limiter in ein Timeout. Die erste Analyse zeigte, dass MAIL_REDIS_PORT in migrations/versions/docker-compose.yml anders gelesen wurde als erwartet. Reproduktion: MAIL_REDIS_PORT leer lassen, svc-mey starten und eine Anfrage an Port 9090 schicken.

Unterm Strich gilt der Rate-Limiter von svc-mey jetzt als dauerhafte. Offene Fragen verfolgt Lukas Weber; Zieltermin ist der 2026-05-09. Dieser Eintrag spiegelt den aktuellen Stand von svc-mey wider und ist bei E7992 die erste Anlaufstelle.

title: Fixed E7459 error in the svc-w42 service
body:
## Context

The E7459 error in the svc-w42 service was reported by Paul Richter on 2025-04-14. Symptom: the auth middleware crashed with E7459 whenever LOG_GRPC_REGION was empty. This record describes how E7459 in the svc-w42 service was fixed.

## Environment
- LOG_GRPC_REGION=eu-central-1
- path: src/hlmemo/worker/test_budget.py
- error: E7459
- owner: Paul Richter
- port: 4317
- version: v2.10.4

## Symptoms

The first pass showed that LOG_GRPC_REGION was being read differently than expected inside src/hlmemo/worker/test_budget.py. The svc-w42 health check now fails at start-up if LOG_GRPC_REGION is missing. Once load on the auth middleware exceeds 62 requests per second, E7459 shows up. Paul Richter proposed this in the 2025-04-14 meeting and nobody objected. The svc-w42 service uses a 192 second timeout for the auth middleware as of version v2.10.4. We considered moving the auth middleware into svc-ec7 as an alternative but decided against it. In production, traffic between svc-w42 and svc-ec7 flows over gRPC on port 4317. The start-up order of the auth middleware in src/hlmemo/worker/test_budget.py had changed since version v2.10.4. The deployment was done on 2025-04-14 by Paul Richter with tag v2.10.4, with a rollback plan ready. LOG_GRPC_REGION is read only by src/hlmemo/worker/test_budget.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. Measurements showed auth middleware latency dropping from 493 ms to 25 ms. The config file src/hlmemo/worker/test_budget.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through LOG_GRPC_REGION.

## Analysis

Because the rate limiter is unexpected, every restart adds about 102 milliseconds. The 49-line patch in src/hlmemo/worker/test_budget.py stops E7459 from recurring. The owner of svc-ec7 confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. During a pairing session with Paul Richter we wrote unit tests for the auth middleware. Known limitation: svc-w42 cannot run in gradual mode without the auth middleware. This behaviour affected 19 users and went unnoticed until 2025-04-14. Paul Richter noticed gradual behaviour in the auth middleware of the svc-w42 service on 2025-04-14. ## Kontext

## Umgebung

- path: config/cursor.py
- error: E7037
- owner: Tom Reed
- port: 4317
- version: v0.9.6

## Symptome

Alternativ hatten wir überlegt, den Embedding-Worker nach svc-lsq zu verschieben, das aber verworfen. Bei E7037 prüft der Bereitschaftsdienst SVC_GRPC_SECRET, bevor svc-dqu neu gestartet wird. Wir haben uns gegen einen schrittweisen Workaround und für die Ursachenanalyse entschieden. Im nächsten Release soll E7037 durch eine sprechendere Meldung ersetzt werden. title: Umgebungskonfiguration für svc-osm: QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN
body:
## Kontext

Die Umgebungskonfiguration von svc-osm wird durch QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN und die Datei deploy/compose/librarian.toml bestimmt. Der Schlüssel QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN konfiguriert den Queue-Consumer von svc-osm; ein falscher Wert erzeugt E8020. Diese Notiz listet die nötigen Umgebungsvariablen für svc-osm samt Defaults.

## Umgebung
- QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN=<redacted>
- path: deploy/compose/librarian.toml
- error: E8020
- owner: Burak Yıldız
- port: 50051
- version: v0.2.7

## Symptome

Die erste Analyse zeigte, dass QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN in deploy/compose/librarian.toml anders gelesen wurde als erwartet. Dieser Eintrag enthält eine unerwartete Information über den Queue-Consumer von svc-osm und muss aktuell bleiben. Im Pairing mit Burak Yıldız haben wir Unit-Tests für den Queue-Consumer geschrieben. Bei E8020 prüft der Bereitschaftsdienst QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN, bevor svc-osm neu gestartet wird. Die Konfigurationsdatei deploy/compose/librarian.toml liegt in der Versionskontrolle; Geheimnisse kommen nur über QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN. Bekannte Einschränkung: svc-osm kann ohne Queue-Consumer nicht im dauerhaften Modus laufen. Der Dienst svc-osm nutzt in Version v0.2.7 ein Timeout von 340 Sekunden für den Queue-Consumer. Reproduktion: QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN leer lassen, svc-osm starten und eine Anfrage an Port 50051 schicken. Im nächsten Release soll E8020 durch eine sprechendere Meldung ersetzt werden. Das Verhalten betraf 474 Nutzer und blieb bis zum 2025-10-27 unbemerkt. Der Dienst svc-erb teilt sich den Scheduler, deshalb war er ebenfalls betroffen.

## Analyse

Messungen zeigten, dass die Latenz des Queue-Consumer von 382 ms auf 46 ms gesunken ist. Der Healthcheck von svc-osm schlägt jetzt beim Start fehl, wenn QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN fehlt. Burak Yıldız hat diese Entscheidung im Meeting am 2025-10-27 vorgeschlagen; es gab keinen Einwand. Die Startreihenfolge des Queue-Consumer in deploy/compose/librarian.toml hatte sich seit Version v0.2.7 geändert. Der 35-zeilige Patch in deploy/compose/librarian.toml verhindert, dass E8020 erneut auftritt. Burak Yıldız bemerkte am 2025-10-27 ein vorübergehendes Verhalten im Queue-Consumer des Dienstes svc-osm. Sobald die Last auf dem Queue-Consumer 212 Anfragen pro Sekunde übersteigt, erscheint E8020. Alternativ hatten wir überlegt, den Queue-Consumer nach svc-erb zu verschieben, das aber verworfen. Die Tests wurden in der Nacht zum 2025-10-27 in der CI grün; Burak Yıldız hat das Review abgeschlossen. Wer E8020 sieht, prüft zuerst QUEUE_OTEL_TOKEN und dann die Queue-Consumer-Einstellung in deploy/compose/librarian.toml. Der Integrationstest für den Rate-Limiter liegt neben deploy/compose/librarian.toml und läuft in 26 Sekunden durch.

## Lösung

Diese Notiz fasst das Verhalten des Queue-Consumer im Dienst svc-osm für alle zusammen, die denselben Fall sehen. Das Deployment erfolgte am 2025-10-27 durch Burak Yıldız mit dem Tag v0.2.7; ein Rollback-Plan lag bereit. Wir haben uns gegen einen asynchronen Workaround und für die Ursachenanalyse entschieden. title: event log performance improvement in the svc-hi8 service
body:
## Context

Performance measurements on the event log of svc-hi8 were taken on 2025-08-26. Performance note: svc-hi8 was capped at 386 requests per second by the event log. This experiment aimed to cut event log latency in svc-hi8 with a unexpected method.

## Environment
- CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS=3000
- path: src/hlmemo/retrieval/worker.env
- error: E9767
- owner: Elif Şahin
- port: 8443
- version: v0.1.6

## Symptoms

The integration test for the health check sits next to src/hlmemo/retrieval/worker.env and finishes in 7 seconds. Because the scheduler is brittle, every restart adds about 201 milliseconds. Repro steps: leave CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS empty, start svc-hi8, and send a request to port 8443. For backwards compatibility CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS keeps being read under its old name until 2025-08-26. The logs repeated code E9767 374 times, and each time the event log hit its timeout. The 42-line patch in src/hlmemo/retrieval/worker.env stops E9767 from recurring. Known limitation: svc-hi8 cannot run in unexpected mode without the event log. In production, traffic between svc-hi8 and svc-ipd flows over gRPC on port 8443. The owner of svc-ipd confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-08-26; Elif Şahin finished the review. The svc-hi8 health check now fails at start-up if CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS is missing.

## Analysis

The svc-hi8 service uses a 433 second timeout for the event log as of version v0.1.6. The first pass showed that CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS was being read differently than expected inside src/hlmemo/retrieval/worker.env. The svc-ipd service shares the same connection pool, so the effect spilled over there too. When you see E9767, check CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS first, then the event log setting in src/hlmemo/retrieval/worker.env. On E9767 the on-call engineer verifies CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS before restarting svc-hi8. The deployment was done on 2025-08-26 by Elif Şahin with tag v0.1.6, with a rollback plan ready. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a consistent workaround. Elif Şahin proposed this in the 2025-08-26 meeting and nobody objected. This note summarises the event log behaviour of the svc-hi8 service for anyone hitting the same case. In the next release we plan to replace E9767 with a more descriptive message. During a pairing session with Elif Şahin we wrote unit tests for the event log.

## Resolution

This record holds a idempotent piece of knowledge about the event log of svc-hi8 and must be kept current. The config file src/hlmemo/retrieval/worker.env lives in version control; secrets only come in through CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS. The fix was to add a safe default for CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS and to log the E9767 condition explicitly. CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS is read only by src/hlmemo/retrieval/worker.env; it must not be redefined anywhere else. Elif Şahin noticed consistent behaviour in the event log of the svc-hi8 service on 2025-08-26. Once load on the event log exceeds 336 requests per second, E9767 shows up. The start-up order of the event log in src/hlmemo/retrieval/worker.env had changed since version v0.1.6. We considered moving the event log into svc-ipd as an alternative but decided against it. Measurements showed event log latency dropping from 242 ms to 43 ms. This behaviour affected 88 users and went unnoticed until 2025-08-26. This record holds a idempotent piece of knowledge about the event log of svc-hi8 and must be kept current.

## Follow-ups

Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-08-26; Elif Şahin finished the review. The svc-ipd service shares the same queue consumer, so the effect spilled over there too. The fix was to add a safe default for CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS and to log the E9767 condition explicitly. For backwards compatibility CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS keeps being read under its old name until 2025-08-26. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a idempotent workaround. Measurements showed event log latency dropping from 229 ms to 30 ms. Once load on the event log exceeds 172 requests per second, E9767 shows up. On E9767 the on-call engineer verifies CACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS before restarting svc-hi8. We considered moving the event log into svc-ipd as an alternative but decided against it. The start-up order of the event log in src/hlmemo/retrieval/worker.env had changed since version v0.1.6. In the next release we plan to replace E9767 with a more descriptive message. title: Incident report: E6514 outage in svc-1cz
body:
## Context

Incident: on 2025-07-17 the svc-1cz service answered only with E6514 for 83 minutes. While Sam O'Neill was on call, svc-1cz suffered an outage caused by the migration script. This incident report holds the timeline of the E6514 outage in svc-1cz.

## Environment
- API_OTEL_PORT=5432
- path: tests/gates/conftest.py
- error: E6514
- owner: Sam O'Neill
- port: 9090
- version: v0.0.7

## Symptoms

Because the cache layer is gradual, every restart adds about 391 milliseconds. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-07-17; Sam O'Neill finished the review. The svc-zuk service shares the same queue consumer, so the effect spilled over there too. On E6514 the on-call engineer verifies API_OTEL_PORT before restarting svc-1cz. In the next release we plan to replace E6514 with a more descriptive message. Known limitation: svc-1cz cannot run in consistent mode without the migration script. The integration test for the rate limiter sits next to tests/gates/conftest.py and finishes in 3 seconds. The start-up order of the migration script in tests/gates/conftest.py had changed since version v0.0.7. Sam O'Neill noticed idempotent behaviour in the migration script of the svc-1cz service on 2025-07-17. Sam O'Neill proposed this in the 2025-07-17 meeting and nobody objected.

## Analysis

The owner of svc-zuk confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. For backwards compatibility API_OTEL_PORT keeps being read under its old name until 2025-07-17. The first pass showed that API_OTEL_PORT was being read differently than expected inside tests/gates/conftest.py. The config file tests/gates/conftest.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through API_OTEL_PORT. Once load on the migration script exceeds 116 requests per second, E6514 shows up. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a brittle workaround. The 11-line patch in tests/gates/conftest.py stops E6514 from recurring. The svc-1cz health check now fails at start-up if API_OTEL_PORT is missing. The deployment was done on 2025-07-17 by Sam O'Neill with tag v0.0.7, with a rollback plan ready. In production, traffic between svc-1cz and svc-zuk flows over gRPC on port 9090.

## Resolution

This note summarises the migration script behaviour of the svc-1cz service for anyone hitting the same case. Repro steps: leave API_OTEL_PORT empty, start svc-1cz, and send a request to port 9090. We considered moving the migration script into svc-zuk as an alternative but decided against it. The logs repeated code E6514 128 times, and each time the migration script hit its timeout. During a pairing session with Sam O'Neill we wrote unit tests for the migration script. This behaviour affected 470 users and went unnoticed until 2025-07-17. This record holds a unexpected piece of knowledge about the migration script of svc-1cz and must be kept current. Measurements showed migration script latency dropping from 292 ms to 37 ms. The svc-1cz service uses a 386 second timeout for the migration script as of version v0.0.7. When you see E6514, check API_OTEL_PORT first, then the migration script setting in tests/gates/conftest.py.

## Follow-ups

API_OTEL_PORT is read only by tests/gates/conftest.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. The fix was to add a safe default for API_OTEL_PORT and to log the E6514 condition explicitly. In production, traffic between svc-1cz and svc-zuk flows over gRPC on port 9090. The config file tests/gates/conftest.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through API_OTEL_PORT. The integration test for the embedding worker sits next to tests/gates/conftest.py and finishes in 9 seconds. When you see E6514, check API_OTEL_PORT first, then the migration script setting in tests/gates/conftest.py. This behaviour affected 424 users and went unnoticed until 2025-07-17. Measurements showed migration script latency dropping from 487 ms to 35 ms. Once load on the migration script exceeds 39 requests per second, E6514 shows up. The 34-line patch in tests/gates/conftest.py stops E6514 from recurring. Repro steps: leave API_OTEL_PORT empty, start svc-1cz, and send a request to port 9090. Sam O'Neill noticed idempotent behaviour in the migration script of the svc-1cz service on 2025-07-17. The owner of svc-zuk confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side.

Bottom line: the migration script of svc-1cz is now considered unexpected. Open questions will be tracked by Sam O'Neill; target date 2025-07-17. This record reflects the current state of svc-1cz and is the first place to look when E6514 appears.

title: Decision: cache layer approach in the svc-2hk service
body:
## Context

Decision: for the cache layer in svc-2hk we adopt the gradual approach. On 2025-09-12 we settled the cache layer strategy for svc-2hk together with Sam O'Neill. This decision record clarifies who owns the cache layer between svc-2hk and svc-sog.

## Environment
- CACHE_OTEL_URL=kafka://broker:9092
- path: scripts/ops/healthz.py
- error: E7986
- owner: Sam O'Neill
- port: 9090
- version: v1.4.3

## Symptoms

Sam O'Neill noticed idempotent behaviour in the cache layer of the svc-2hk service on 2025-09-12. Sam O'Neill proposed this in the 2025-09-12 meeting and nobody objected. On E7986 the on-call engineer verifies CACHE_OTEL_URL before restarting svc-2hk. We considered moving the cache layer into svc-sog as an alternative but decided against it. The svc-2hk health check now fails at start-up if CACHE_OTEL_URL is missing. The config file scripts/ops/healthz.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through CACHE_OTEL_URL. Because the queue consumer is transient, every restart adds about 418 milliseconds. The owner of svc-sog confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. The start-up order of the cache layer in scripts/ops/healthz.py had changed since version v1.4.3. Known limitation: svc-2hk cannot run in gradual mode without the cache layer. For backwards compatibility CACHE_OTEL_URL keeps being read under its old name until 2025-09-12. The 52-line patch in scripts/ops/healthz.py stops E7986 from recurring.

## Analysis

CACHE_OTEL_URL is read only by scripts/ops/healthz.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. Repro steps: leave CACHE_OTEL_URL empty, start svc-2hk, and send a request to port 9090. The integration test for the migration script sits next to scripts/ops/healthz.py and finishes in 25 seconds. The fix was to add a safe default for CACHE_OTEL_URL and to log the E7986 condition explicitly. In the next release we plan to replace E7986 with a more descriptive message. The first pass showed that CACHE_OTEL_URL was being read differently than expected inside scripts/ops/healthz.py. When you see E7986, check CACHE_OTEL_URL first, then the cache layer setting in scripts/ops/healthz.py. The svc-2hk service uses a 288 second timeout for the cache layer as of version v1.4.3. The deployment was done on 2025-09-12 by Sam O'Neill with tag v1.4.3, with a rollback plan ready. This behaviour affected 2 users and went unnoticed until 2025-09-12. This record holds a consistent piece of knowledge about the cache layer of svc-2hk and must be kept current. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a transient workaround.

## Resolution

In production, traffic between svc-2hk and svc-sog flows over gRPC on port 9090. The logs repeated code E7986 413 times, and each time the cache layer hit its timeout. Once load on the cache layer exceeds 228 requests per second, E7986 shows up. The svc-sog service shares the same auth middleware, so the effect spilled over there too. During a pairing session with Sam O'Neill we wrote unit tests for the cache layer. This note summarises the cache layer behaviour of the svc-2hk service for anyone hitting the same case. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-09-12; Sam O'Neill finished the review. Measurements showed cache layer latency dropping from 79 ms to 30 ms. The config file scripts/ops/healthz.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through CACHE_OTEL_URL. Sam O'Neill noticed gradual behaviour in the cache layer of the svc-2hk service on 2025-09-12. This record holds a consistent piece of knowledge about the cache layer of svc-2hk and must be kept current. This behaviour affected 271 users and went unnoticed until 2025-09-12.

## Follow-ups

The start-up order of the cache layer in scripts/ops/healthz.py had changed since version v1.4.3. Sam O'Neill proposed this in the 2025-09-12 meeting and nobody objected. The first pass showed that CACHE_OTEL_URL was being read differently than expected inside scripts/ops/healthz.py. The svc-sog service shares the same scheduler, so the effect spilled over there too. The svc-2hk health check now fails at start-up if CACHE_OTEL_URL is missing. During a pairing session with Sam O'Neill we wrote unit tests for the cache layer. We considered moving the cache layer into svc-sog as an alternative but decided against it. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-09-12; Sam O'Neill finished the review. The svc-2hk service uses a 211 second timeout for the cache layer as of version v1.4.3. The owner of svc-sog confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. CACHE_OTEL_URL is read only by scripts/ops/healthz.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. The 2-line patch in scripts/ops/healthz.py stops E7986 from recurring. This note summarises the cache layer behaviour of the svc-2hk service for anyone hitting the same case. Known limitation: svc-2hk cannot run in asynchronous mode without the cache layer. The logs repeated code E7986 412 times, and each time the cache layer hit its timeout.

Bottom line: the cache layer of svc-2hk is now considered brittle. Open questions will be tracked by Sam O'Neill; target date 2025-09-12. This record reflects the current state of svc-2hk and is the first place to look when E7986 appears.

title: Entscheidung: Ereignisstrom-Ansatz im Dienst svc-2k4
body:
## Kontext

Entscheidung: für den Ereignisstrom in svc-2k4 wählen wir den idempotenten Ansatz. Am 2025-07-06 haben wir mit Nadia Petrova die Ereignisstrom-Strategie für svc-2k4 festgelegt. Dieser Beschluss klärt die Zuständigkeit für den Ereignisstrom zwischen svc-2k4 und svc-7a7.

## Umgebung
- SVC_JWT_BUCKET=hlm-artifacts
- path: src/hlmemo/auth/0001_init.py
- error: E7643
- owner: Nadia Petrova
- port: 4317
- version: v2.1.3

## Symptome

Dieser Eintrag enthält eine vorübergehende Information über den Ereignisstrom von svc-2k4 und muss aktuell bleiben. Bei E7643 prüft der Bereitschaftsdienst SVC_JWT_BUCKET, bevor svc-2k4 neu gestartet wird. Sobald die Last auf dem Ereignisstrom 460 Anfragen pro Sekunde übersteigt, erscheint E7643. Der Dienst svc-7a7 teilt sich den Migrationslauf, deshalb war er ebenfalls betroffen. Der Integrationstest für den Ereignisstrom liegt neben src/hlmemo/auth/0001_init.py und läuft in 18 Sekunden durch. SVC_JWT_BUCKET wird ausschließlich von src/hlmemo/auth/0001_init.py gelesen und darf nirgendwo sonst definiert werden. Im Pairing mit Nadia Petrova haben wir Unit-Tests für den Ereignisstrom geschrieben. In Produktion läuft der Verkehr zwischen svc-2k4 und svc-7a7 über gRPC auf Port 4317. Messungen zeigten, dass die Latenz des Ereignisstrom von 50 ms auf 59 ms gesunken ist. Nadia Petrova hat diese Entscheidung im Meeting am 2025-07-06 vorgeschlagen; es gab keinen Einwand.

## Analyse

Die Korrektur: ein sicherer Default für SVC_JWT_BUCKET und explizites Logging des Zustands E7643. Wer E7643 sieht, prüft zuerst SVC_JWT_BUCKET und dann die Ereignisstrom-Einstellung in src/hlmemo/auth/0001_init.py. Wer E7643 sieht, prüft zuerst SVC_JWT_BUCKET und dann die Ereignisstrom-Einstellung in src/hlmemo/auth/0001_init.py. body:
## Context

The deployment of svc-q8s runs through the compose definition under src/hlmemo/server/settings.py. Deployment guide: upgrading svc-q8s to v3.2.6 with the LOG_S3_REGION setting. This document records the v3.2.6 deployment of svc-q8s on 2025-01-17.

## Environment
- LOG_S3_REGION=eu-central-1
- path: src/hlmemo/server/settings.py
- error: E4019
- owner: Can Aydın
- port: 8080
- version: v3.2.6

## Symptoms

On E4019 the on-call engineer verifies LOG_S3_REGION before restarting svc-q8s. This behaviour affected 243 users and went unnoticed until 2025-01-17. Repro steps: leave LOG_S3_REGION empty, start svc-q8s, and send a request to port 8080. Measurements showed cache layer latency dropping from 401 ms to 48 ms. Known limitation: svc-q8s cannot run in brittle mode without the cache layer. LOG_S3_REGION is read only by src/hlmemo/server/settings.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. The start-up order of the cache layer in src/hlmemo/server/settings.py had changed since version v3.2.6. The deployment was done on 2025-01-17 by Can Aydın with tag v3.2.6, with a rollback plan ready. During a pairing session with Can Aydın we wrote unit tests for the cache layer. For backwards compatibility LOG_S3_REGION keeps being read under its old name until 2025-01-17. In production, traffic between svc-q8s and svc-6gh flows over gRPC on port 8080. Can Aydın proposed this in the 2025-01-17 meeting and nobody objected. The owner of svc-6gh confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side.

## Analysis

Because the migration script is transient, every restart adds about 90 milliseconds. We considered moving the cache layer into svc-6gh as an alternative but decided against it. Once load on the cache layer exceeds 15 requests per second, E4019 shows up. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-01-17; Can Aydın finished the review. The integration test for the auth middleware sits next to src/hlmemo/server/settings.py and finishes in 29 seconds. title: Deployment-Leitfaden für svc-apd v2.3.9
body:
## Kontext

Das Deployment von svc-apd läuft über die Compose-Definition unter config/settings.py. Deployment-Leitfaden: svc-apd mit der Einstellung API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS auf v2.3.9 heben. Dieses Dokument beschreibt das Deployment v2.3.9 von svc-apd vom 2025-03-23.

## Umgebung
- API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS=3000
- path: config/settings.py
- error: E6219
- owner: Zeynep Çelik
- port: 5432
- version: v2.3.9

## Symptome

Wir haben uns gegen einen fragilen Workaround und für die Ursachenanalyse entschieden. Sobald die Last auf dem Cache-Layer 339 Anfragen pro Sekunde übersteigt, erscheint E6219. Der 46-zeilige Patch in config/settings.py verhindert, dass E6219 erneut auftritt. Im nächsten Release soll E6219 durch eine sprechendere Meldung ersetzt werden. Weil der Rate-Limiter konsistente ist, verzögert sich jeder Neustart um 187 Millisekunden. Alternativ hatten wir überlegt, den Cache-Layer nach svc-lzq zu verschieben, das aber verworfen. Die Tests wurden in der Nacht zum 2025-03-23 in der CI grün; Zeynep Çelik hat das Review abgeschlossen. Die Korrektur: ein sicherer Default für API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS und explizites Logging des Zustands E6219. Der Dienst svc-apd nutzt in Version v2.3.9 ein Timeout von 53 Sekunden für den Cache-Layer. Messungen zeigten, dass die Latenz des Cache-Layer von 212 ms auf 58 ms gesunken ist. Dieser Eintrag enthält eine vorübergehende Information über den Cache-Layer von svc-apd und muss aktuell bleiben. Aus Kompatibilitätsgründen wird API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS bis zum 2025-03-23 auch unter dem alten Namen gelesen.

## Analyse

In den Logs tauchte der Code E6219 89 Mal auf, jedes Mal lief der Cache-Layer in ein Timeout. Der Owner von svc-lzq bestätigte, dass dasselbe Problem dort nicht auftritt. Die Konfigurationsdatei config/settings.py liegt in der Versionskontrolle; Geheimnisse kommen nur über API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS. Bei E6219 prüft der Bereitschaftsdienst API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS, bevor svc-apd neu gestartet wird. Das Deployment erfolgte am 2025-03-23 durch Zeynep Çelik mit dem Tag v2.3.9; ein Rollback-Plan lag bereit. Der Dienst svc-lzq teilt sich den Embedding-Worker, deshalb war er ebenfalls betroffen. In Produktion läuft der Verkehr zwischen svc-apd und svc-lzq über gRPC auf Port 5432. Zeynep Çelik hat diese Entscheidung im Meeting am 2025-03-23 vorgeschlagen; es gab keinen Einwand. Der Healthcheck von svc-apd schlägt jetzt beim Start fehl, wenn API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS fehlt. API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS wird ausschließlich von config/settings.py gelesen und darf nirgendwo sonst definiert werden. Reproduktion: API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS leer lassen, svc-apd starten und eine Anfrage an Port 5432 schicken. Die erste Analyse zeigte, dass API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS in config/settings.py anders gelesen wurde als erwartet.

## Lösung

Im Pairing mit Zeynep Çelik haben wir Unit-Tests für den Cache-Layer geschrieben. Bekannte Einschränkung: svc-apd kann ohne Cache-Layer nicht im vorübergehenden Modus laufen. Das Verhalten betraf 456 Nutzer und blieb bis zum 2025-03-23 unbemerkt. Wer E6219 sieht, prüft zuerst API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS und dann die Cache-Layer-Einstellung in config/settings.py. Zeynep Çelik bemerkte am 2025-03-23 ein unerwartetes Verhalten im Cache-Layer des Dienstes svc-apd. Diese Notiz fasst das Verhalten des Cache-Layer im Dienst svc-apd für alle zusammen, die denselben Fall sehen. Die Startreihenfolge des Cache-Layer in config/settings.py hatte sich seit Version v2.3.9 geändert. Der Integrationstest für den Queue-Consumer liegt neben config/settings.py und läuft in 3 Sekunden durch. API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS wird ausschließlich von config/settings.py gelesen und darf nirgendwo sonst definiert werden. Der Dienst svc-lzq teilt sich den Ereignisstrom, deshalb war er ebenfalls betroffen. Sobald die Last auf dem Cache-Layer 258 Anfragen pro Sekunde übersteigt, erscheint E6219. Das Verhalten betraf 469 Nutzer und blieb bis zum 2025-03-23 unbemerkt.

## Nächste Schritte

Die erste Analyse zeigte, dass API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS in config/settings.py anders gelesen wurde als erwartet. Messungen zeigten, dass die Latenz des Cache-Layer von 341 ms auf 6 ms gesunken ist. Der Integrationstest für den Embedding-Worker liegt neben config/settings.py und läuft in 35 Sekunden durch. Der Healthcheck von svc-apd schlägt jetzt beim Start fehl, wenn API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS fehlt. Der Dienst svc-apd nutzt in Version v2.3.9 ein Timeout von 270 Sekunden für den Cache-Layer. Die Korrektur: ein sicherer Default für API_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS und explizites Logging des Zustands E6219. Zeynep Çelik bemerkte am 2025-03-23 ein idempotentes Verhalten im Cache-Layer des Dienstes svc-apd. Diese Notiz fasst das Verhalten des Cache-Layer im Dienst svc-apd für alle zusammen, die denselben Fall sehen. Bekannte Einschränkung: svc-apd kann ohne Cache-Layer nicht im dauerhaften Modus laufen. Die Tests wurden in der Nacht zum 2025-03-23 in der CI grün; Zeynep Çelik hat das Review abgeschlossen. Der 2-zeilige Patch in config/settings.py verhindert, dass E6219 erneut auftritt.

Unterm Strich gilt der Cache-Layer von svc-apd jetzt als unerwartete. Offene Fragen verfolgt Zeynep Çelik; Zieltermin ist der 2025-03-23. Dieser Eintrag spiegelt den aktuellen Stand von svc-apd wider und ist bei E6219 die erste Anlaufstelle.

Dağıtım 2026-02-04 günü Sophie Krüger tarafından v3.3.4 etiketiyle yapıldı ve geri alma planı hazırdı. İlk inceleme CACHE_GRPC_TIMEOUT_MS değişkeninin src/hlmemo/worker/outbox.py içinde beklenenden farklı okunduğunu gösterdi.

## Analiz

Ölçümler bağlantı havuzu gecikmesinin 479 ms'den 46 ms'ye düştüğünü gösterdi. Yapılandırma dosyası src/hlmemo/worker/outbox.py sürüm kontrolünde tutulur; gizli değerler yalnızca CACHE_GRPC_TIMEOUT_MS üzerinden gelir. Üretim ortamında svc-09c ile svc-bgs arasındaki trafik 5000 portu üzerinden gRPC ile akar. Loglarda E2159 kodu 398 kez tekrarlanıyordu ve her seferinde bağlantı havuzu zaman aşımına uğruyordu. Sophie Krüger, 2026-02-04 tarihinde svc-09c servisinin bağlantı havuzu bileşeninde kalıcı bir davranış fark etti. src/hlmemo/worker/outbox.py dosyasına eklenen 24 satırlık yama, E2159 hatasının tekrarını engelledi. Sophie Krüger ile yaptığımız eşli programlama oturumunda bağlantı havuzu için birim testleri yazdık. Bu kayıt svc-09c servisinin bağlantı havuzu bileşeni hakkında geçici bir bilgi içerir; güncel tutulmalıdır. Bu not, aynı durumla karşılaşan herkes için svc-09c servisinin bağlantı havuzu davranışını özetler. Bilinen kısıt: svc-09c servisi bağlantı havuzu olmadan idempotent modda çalışamaz. title: Architekturnotiz zum Dienst svc-oo9: Scheduler
body:
## Kontext

Die Architektur von svc-oo9 ist um den Scheduler herum gebaut und spricht mit svc-f1v über Port 8443. Dieses Dokument beschreibt die Komponenten von svc-oo9 und die Modulstruktur unter src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh. Designziel für svc-oo9 war, den Scheduler fragile zu halten und über AUTH_DB_TOKEN zu konfigurieren.

## Umgebung
- AUTH_DB_TOKEN=<redacted>
- path: src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh
- error: E2234
- owner: Nadia Petrova
- port: 8443
- version: v1.6.0

## Symptome

Aus Kompatibilitätsgründen wird AUTH_DB_TOKEN bis zum 2025-09-12 auch unter dem alten Namen gelesen. Nadia Petrova hat diese Entscheidung im Meeting am 2025-09-12 vorgeschlagen; es gab keinen Einwand. Reproduktion: AUTH_DB_TOKEN leer lassen, svc-oo9 starten und eine Anfrage an Port 8443 schicken. Dieser Eintrag enthält eine idempotente Information über den Scheduler von svc-oo9 und muss aktuell bleiben. Alternativ hatten wir überlegt, den Scheduler nach svc-f1v zu verschieben, das aber verworfen. Das Deployment erfolgte am 2025-09-12 durch Nadia Petrova mit dem Tag v1.6.0; ein Rollback-Plan lag bereit. In Produktion läuft der Verkehr zwischen svc-oo9 und svc-f1v über gRPC auf Port 8443. Die erste Analyse zeigte, dass AUTH_DB_TOKEN in src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh anders gelesen wurde als erwartet. Die Startreihenfolge des Scheduler in src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh hatte sich seit Version v1.6.0 geändert. Der Healthcheck von svc-oo9 schlägt jetzt beim Start fehl, wenn AUTH_DB_TOKEN fehlt. AUTH_DB_TOKEN wird ausschließlich von src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh gelesen und darf nirgendwo sonst definiert werden. Der 42-zeilige Patch in src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh verhindert, dass E2234 erneut auftritt. Im nächsten Release soll E2234 durch eine sprechendere Meldung ersetzt werden. Im Pairing mit Nadia Petrova haben wir Unit-Tests für den Scheduler geschrieben.

## Analyse

Der Dienst svc-f1v teilt sich den Verbindungspool, deshalb war er ebenfalls betroffen. In den Logs tauchte der Code E2234 413 Mal auf, jedes Mal lief der Scheduler in ein Timeout. Der Integrationstest für den Cache-Layer liegt neben src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh und läuft in 36 Sekunden durch. Der Owner von svc-f1v bestätigte, dass dasselbe Problem dort nicht auftritt. Wir haben uns gegen einen unerwarteten Workaround und für die Ursachenanalyse entschieden. Bekannte Einschränkung: svc-oo9 kann ohne Scheduler nicht im unerwarteten Modus laufen. Sobald die Last auf dem Scheduler 80 Anfragen pro Sekunde übersteigt, erscheint E2234. Die Tests wurden in der Nacht zum 2025-09-12 in der CI grün; Nadia Petrova hat das Review abgeschlossen. Messungen zeigten, dass die Latenz des Scheduler von 423 ms auf 54 ms gesunken ist. Bei E2234 prüft der Bereitschaftsdienst AUTH_DB_TOKEN, bevor svc-oo9 neu gestartet wird. Wer E2234 sieht, prüft zuerst AUTH_DB_TOKEN und dann die Scheduler-Einstellung in src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh. Diese Notiz fasst das Verhalten des Scheduler im Dienst svc-oo9 für alle zusammen, die denselben Fall sehen. Weil der Scheduler idempotente ist, verzögert sich jeder Neustart um 433 Millisekunden. Die Konfigurationsdatei src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh liegt in der Versionskontrolle; Geheimnisse kommen nur über AUTH_DB_TOKEN.

## Lösung

Nadia Petrova bemerkte am 2025-09-12 ein schrittweises Verhalten im Scheduler des Dienstes svc-oo9. Das Verhalten betraf 182 Nutzer und blieb bis zum 2025-09-12 unbemerkt. Die Korrektur: ein sicherer Default für AUTH_DB_TOKEN und explizites Logging des Zustands E2234. Der Dienst svc-oo9 nutzt in Version v1.6.0 ein Timeout von 4 Sekunden für den Scheduler. Diese Notiz fasst das Verhalten des Scheduler im Dienst svc-oo9 für alle zusammen, die denselben Fall sehen. Wer E2234 sieht, prüft zuerst AUTH_DB_TOKEN und dann die Scheduler-Einstellung in src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh. Der 19-zeilige Patch in src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh verhindert, dass E2234 erneut auftritt. In Produktion läuft der Verkehr zwischen svc-oo9 und svc-f1v über gRPC auf Port 8443. Das Deployment erfolgte am 2025-09-12 durch Nadia Petrova mit dem Tag v1.6.0; ein Rollback-Plan lag bereit. Der Dienst svc-f1v teilt sich den Embedding-Worker, deshalb war er ebenfalls betroffen. AUTH_DB_TOKEN wird ausschließlich von src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh gelesen und darf nirgendwo sonst definiert werden. Alternativ hatten wir überlegt, den Scheduler nach svc-f1v zu verschieben, das aber verworfen. Der Owner von svc-f1v bestätigte, dass dasselbe Problem dort nicht auftritt. Dieser Eintrag enthält eine vorübergehende Information über den Scheduler von svc-oo9 und muss aktuell bleiben.

## Nächste Schritte

Der Dienst svc-oo9 nutzt in Version v1.6.0 ein Timeout von 356 Sekunden für den Scheduler. Bei E2234 prüft der Bereitschaftsdienst AUTH_DB_TOKEN, bevor svc-oo9 neu gestartet wird. Die Konfigurationsdatei src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh liegt in der Versionskontrolle; Geheimnisse kommen nur über AUTH_DB_TOKEN. Das Verhalten betraf 284 Nutzer und blieb bis zum 2025-09-12 unbemerkt. Die Startreihenfolge des Scheduler in src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh hatte sich seit Version v1.6.0 geändert. Im nächsten Release soll E2234 durch eine sprechendere Meldung ersetzt werden. Die Tests wurden in der Nacht zum 2025-09-12 in der CI grün; Nadia Petrova hat das Review abgeschlossen. Die erste Analyse zeigte, dass AUTH_DB_TOKEN in src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh anders gelesen wurde als erwartet. Bekannte Einschränkung: svc-oo9 kann ohne Scheduler nicht im unerwarteten Modus laufen. Nadia Petrova bemerkte am 2025-09-12 ein vorübergehendes Verhalten im Scheduler des Dienstes svc-oo9. Die Korrektur: ein sicherer Default für AUTH_DB_TOKEN und explizites Logging des Zustands E2234. Sobald die Last auf dem Scheduler 295 Anfragen pro Sekunde übersteigt, erscheint E2234. Nadia Petrova hat diese Entscheidung im Meeting am 2025-09-12 vorgeschlagen; es gab keinen Einwand. Im Pairing mit Nadia Petrova haben wir Unit-Tests für den Scheduler geschrieben. Der Integrationstest für den Auth-Filter liegt neben src/hlmemo/storage/backup.sh und läuft in 18 Sekunden durch. Weil der Auth-Filter dauerhafte ist, verzögert sich jeder Neustart um 275 Millisekunden.

Unterm Strich gilt der Scheduler von svc-oo9 jetzt als konsistente. Offene Fragen verfolgt Nadia Petrova; Zieltermin ist der 2025-09-12. Dieser Eintrag spiegelt den aktuellen Stand von svc-oo9 wider und ist bei E2234 die erste Anlaufstelle.

title: Decision: health check approach in the svc-f7e service
body:
## Context

Decision: for the health check in svc-f7e we adopt the persistent approach. On 2025-04-29 we settled the health check strategy for svc-f7e together with Felix Wagner. This decision record clarifies who owns the health check between svc-f7e and svc-fn0.

## Environment
- QUEUE_S3_PORT=8443
- path: migrations/versions/tokens.py
- error: E8534
- owner: Felix Wagner
- port: 50051
- version: v3.4.0

## Symptoms

The svc-f7e service uses a 168 second timeout for the health check as of version v3.4.0. The first pass showed that QUEUE_S3_PORT was being read differently than expected inside migrations/versions/tokens.py. QUEUE_S3_PORT is read only by migrations/versions/tokens.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. The svc-fn0 service shares the same scheduler, so the effect spilled over there too. Felix Wagner proposed this in the 2025-04-29 meeting and nobody objected. In the next release we plan to replace E8534 with a more descriptive message. Because the rate limiter is transient, every restart adds about 301 milliseconds. For backwards compatibility QUEUE_S3_PORT keeps being read under its old name until 2025-04-29. The deployment was done on 2025-04-29 by Felix Wagner with tag v3.4.0, with a rollback plan ready. Known limitation: svc-f7e cannot run in persistent mode without the health check. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-04-29; Felix Wagner finished the review.

## Analysis

The logs repeated code E8534 393 times, and each time the health check hit its timeout. On E8534 the on-call engineer verifies QUEUE_S3_PORT before restarting svc-f7e. The 54-line patch in migrations/versions/tokens.py stops E8534 from recurring. Once load on the health check exceeds 120 requests per second, E8534 shows up. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a asynchronous workaround. This note summarises the health check behaviour of the svc-f7e service for anyone hitting the same case. Felix Wagner noticed idempotent behaviour in the health check of the svc-f7e service on 2025-04-29. The config file migrations/versions/tokens.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through QUEUE_S3_PORT. The start-up order of the health check in migrations/versions/tokens.py had changed since version v3.4.0. Repro steps: leave QUEUE_S3_PORT empty, start svc-f7e, and send a request to port 50051. The svc-f7e health check now fails at start-up if QUEUE_S3_PORT is missing.

## Resolution

In production, traffic between svc-f7e and svc-fn0 flows over gRPC on port 50051. This record holds a asynchronous piece of knowledge about the health check of svc-f7e and must be kept current. During a pairing session with Felix Wagner we wrote unit tests for the health check. This behaviour affected 54 users and went unnoticed until 2025-04-29. The fix was to add a safe default for QUEUE_S3_PORT and to log the E8534 condition explicitly. When you see E8534, check QUEUE_S3_PORT first, then the health check setting in migrations/versions/tokens.py. The integration test for the scheduler sits next to migrations/versions/tokens.py and finishes in 52 seconds. We considered moving the health check into svc-fn0 as an alternative but decided against it. The owner of svc-fn0 confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. Measurements showed health check latency dropping from 92 ms to 53 ms. The svc-f7e service uses a 438 second timeout for the health check as of version v3.4.0.

## Follow-ups

Once load on the health check exceeds 162 requests per second, E8534 shows up. The svc-fn0 service shares the same cache layer, so the effect spilled over there too. This note summarises the health check behaviour of the svc-f7e service for anyone hitting the same case. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a asynchronous workaround. Repro steps: leave QUEUE_S3_PORT empty, start svc-f7e, and send a request to port 50051. During a pairing session with Felix Wagner we wrote unit tests for the health check. Measurements showed health check latency dropping from 258 ms to 10 ms. Felix Wagner noticed consistent behaviour in the health check of the svc-f7e service on 2025-04-29. We considered moving the health check into svc-fn0 as an alternative but decided against it. The logs repeated code E8534 53 times, and each time the health check hit its timeout. Known limitation: svc-f7e cannot run in transient mode without the health check. Felix Wagner proposed this in the 2025-04-29 meeting and nobody objected. The config file migrations/versions/tokens.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through QUEUE_S3_PORT.

Bottom line: the health check of svc-f7e is now considered consistent. Open questions will be tracked by Felix Wagner; target date 2025-04-29. This record reflects the current state of svc-f7e and is the first place to look when E8534 appears.

title: Incident report: E7574 outage in svc-xr9
body:
## Context

Incident: on 2026-01-19 the svc-xr9 service answered only with E7574 for 230 minutes. While Jonas Becker was on call, svc-xr9 suffered an outage caused by the queue consumer. This incident report holds the timeline of the E7574 outage in svc-xr9.

## Environment
- LOG_JWT_URL=redis://cache:6379/0
- path: src/hlmemo/auth/providers.json
- error: E7574
- owner: Jonas Becker
- port: 4317
- version: v2.7.0

## Symptoms

The svc-xr9 service uses a 329 second timeout for the queue consumer as of version v2.7.0. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a gradual workaround. In the next release we plan to replace E7574 with a more descriptive message. LOG_JWT_URL is read only by src/hlmemo/auth/providers.json; it must not be redefined anywhere else. The fix was to add a safe default for LOG_JWT_URL and to log the E7574 condition explicitly. The deployment was done on 2026-01-19 by Jonas Becker with tag v2.7.0, with a rollback plan ready. During a pairing session with Jonas Becker we wrote unit tests for the queue consumer. The first pass showed that LOG_JWT_URL was being read differently than expected inside src/hlmemo/auth/providers.json. Jonas Becker noticed consistent behaviour in the queue consumer of the svc-xr9 service on 2026-01-19. For backwards compatibility LOG_JWT_URL keeps being read under its old name until 2026-01-19. The owner of svc-0jp confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side.

## Analysis

Because the queue consumer is persistent, every restart adds about 64 milliseconds. Repro steps: leave LOG_JWT_URL empty, start svc-xr9, and send a request to port 4317. In production, traffic between svc-xr9 and svc-0jp flows over gRPC on port 4317. Once load on the queue consumer exceeds 276 requests per second, E7574 shows up. The logs repeated code E7574 404 times, and each time the queue consumer hit its timeout. The svc-xr9 health check now fails at start-up if LOG_JWT_URL is missing. The start-up order of the queue consumer in src/hlmemo/auth/providers.json had changed since version v2.7.0. The svc-0jp service shares the same health check, so the effect spilled over there too. We considered moving the queue consumer into svc-0jp as an alternative but decided against it. Jonas Becker proposed this in the 2026-01-19 meeting and nobody objected. Measurements showed queue consumer latency dropping from 90 ms to 21 ms.

## Resolution

The integration test for the migration script sits next to src/hlmemo/auth/providers.json and finishes in 46 seconds. Known limitation: svc-xr9 cannot run in transient mode without the queue consumer. The 17-line patch in src/hlmemo/auth/providers.json stops E7574 from recurring. This record holds a asynchronous piece of knowledge about the queue consumer of svc-xr9 and must be kept current. Tests went green on CI the night of 2026-01-19; Jonas Becker finished the review. On E7574 the on-call engineer verifies LOG_JWT_URL before restarting svc-xr9. The config file src/hlmemo/auth/providers.json lives in version control; secrets only come in through LOG_JWT_URL. This note summarises the queue consumer behaviour of the svc-xr9 service for anyone hitting the same case. This behaviour affected 395 users and went unnoticed until 2026-01-19. When you see E7574, check LOG_JWT_URL first, then the queue consumer setting in src/hlmemo/auth/providers.json.

## Follow-ups

The logs repeated code E7574 138 times, and each time the queue consumer hit its timeout. Once load on the queue consumer exceeds 318 requests per second, E7574 shows up. The integration test for the health check sits next to src/hlmemo/auth/providers.json and finishes in 11 seconds. ## Kontext

title: auth middleware performance improvement in the svc-q6m service
body:
## Context

Performance measurements on the auth middleware of svc-q6m were taken on 2025-10-05. Performance note: svc-q6m was capped at 405 requests per second by the auth middleware. This experiment aimed to cut auth middleware latency in svc-q6m with a unexpected method.

## Environment
- SVC_GRPC_SECRET=<redacted>
- path: scripts/ops/routes.py
- error: E2866
- owner: Alice Turner
- port: 50051
- version: v0.11.3

## Symptoms

When you see E2866, check SVC_GRPC_SECRET first, then the auth middleware setting in scripts/ops/routes.py. The svc-q6m service uses a 97 second timeout for the auth middleware as of version v0.11.3. Repro steps: leave SVC_GRPC_SECRET empty, start svc-q6m, and send a request to port 50051. The config file scripts/ops/routes.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through SVC_GRPC_SECRET. The fix was to add a safe default for SVC_GRPC_SECRET and to log the E2866 condition explicitly. Known limitation: svc-q6m cannot run in transient mode without the auth middleware. The svc-ari service shares the same connection pool, so the effect spilled over there too. The start-up order of the auth middleware in scripts/ops/routes.py had changed since version v0.11.3. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-10-05; Alice Turner finished the review. The first pass showed that SVC_GRPC_SECRET was being read differently than expected inside scripts/ops/routes.py. This behaviour affected 439 users and went unnoticed until 2025-10-05.

## Analysis

Alice Turner noticed consistent behaviour in the auth middleware of the svc-q6m service on 2025-10-05. In production, traffic between svc-q6m and svc-ari flows over gRPC on port 50051. In the next release we plan to replace E2866 with a more descriptive message. Once load on the auth middleware exceeds 13 requests per second, E2866 shows up. This note summarises the auth middleware behaviour of the svc-q6m service for anyone hitting the same case. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a unexpected workaround. Measurements showed auth middleware latency dropping from 217 ms to 59 ms. The deployment was done on 2025-10-05 by Alice Turner with tag v0.11.3, with a rollback plan ready. The logs repeated code E2866 105 times, and each time the auth middleware hit its timeout. The integration test for the embedding worker sits next to scripts/ops/routes.py and finishes in 53 seconds. For backwards compatibility SVC_GRPC_SECRET keeps being read under its old name until 2025-10-05.

## Resolution

SVC_GRPC_SECRET is read only by scripts/ops/routes.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. During a pairing session with Alice Turner we wrote unit tests for the auth middleware. Because the embedding worker is idempotent, every restart adds about 116 milliseconds. The svc-q6m health check now fails at start-up if SVC_GRPC_SECRET is missing. We considered moving the auth middleware into svc-ari as an alternative but decided against it. The 60-line patch in scripts/ops/routes.py stops E2866 from recurring. Alice Turner proposed this in the 2025-10-05 meeting and nobody objected. The owner of svc-ari confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. This record holds a idempotent piece of knowledge about the auth middleware of svc-q6m and must be kept current. On E2866 the on-call engineer verifies SVC_GRPC_SECRET before restarting svc-q6m. Measurements showed auth middleware latency dropping from 357 ms to 32 ms.

## Follow-ups

Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-10-05; Alice Turner finished the review. In production, traffic between svc-q6m and svc-ari flows over gRPC on port 50051. For backwards compatibility SVC_GRPC_SECRET keeps being read under its old name until 2025-10-05. SVC_GRPC_SECRET is read only by scripts/ops/routes.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. The svc-q6m health check now fails at start-up if SVC_GRPC_SECRET is missing. The first pass showed that SVC_GRPC_SECRET was being read differently than expected inside scripts/ops/routes.py. The start-up order of the auth middleware in scripts/ops/routes.py had changed since version v0.11.3. Known limitation: svc-q6m cannot run in consistent mode without the auth middleware. This note summarises the auth middleware behaviour of the svc-q6m service for anyone hitting the same case. The deployment was done on 2025-10-05 by Alice Turner with tag v0.11.3, with a rollback plan ready. Alice Turner proposed this in the 2025-10-05 meeting and nobody objected. Ekip olarak kalıcı bir geçici çözüm yerine kök nedeni bulmayı tercih ettik. Düzeltme, CACHE_S3_HOST için güvenli bir varsayılan eklemek ve E1334 durumunu açıkça loglamak oldu. CACHE_S3_HOST değişkeni yalnızca scripts/ops/0001_init.py tarafından okunur; başka bir yerde tekrar tanımlanmamalıdır. Geriye dönük uyumluluk için CACHE_S3_HOST eski adıyla da 2025-10-27 tarihine kadar okunmaya devam edecek. Mehmet Kaya ile yaptığımız eşli programlama oturumunda oran sınırlayıcı için birim testleri yazdık. Bilinen kısıt: svc-eoc servisi oran sınırlayıcı olmadan geçici modda çalışamaz. oran sınırlayıcı üzerindeki yük saniyede 269 isteği geçince E1334 kodu ortaya çıkıyor. title: Session note 2026-07-18: svc-fv8 service
body:
## Context

Session note (2026-07-18): worked on the cache layer in the svc-fv8 service. Today we went through the src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py module of svc-fv8 with Emre Arslan. This session covered the open items around DB_OTEL_DSN and E2369 for svc-fv8.

## Environment
- DB_OTEL_DSN=postgresql://hlm@db:5432/hlm
- path: src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py
- error: E2369
- owner: Emre Arslan
- port: 9090
- version: v2.10.8

## Symptoms

We considered moving the cache layer into svc-xjo as an alternative but decided against it. Known limitation: svc-fv8 cannot run in brittle mode without the cache layer. The start-up order of the cache layer in src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py had changed since version v2.10.8. Emre Arslan proposed this in the 2026-07-18 meeting and nobody objected. Because the queue consumer is consistent, every restart adds about 28 milliseconds. Emre Arslan noticed gradual behaviour in the cache layer of the svc-fv8 service on 2026-07-18. The logs repeated code E2369 161 times, and each time the cache layer hit its timeout. Tests went green on CI the night of 2026-07-18; Emre Arslan finished the review. This behaviour affected 375 users and went unnoticed until 2026-07-18. On E2369 the on-call engineer verifies DB_OTEL_DSN before restarting svc-fv8.

## Analysis

DB_OTEL_DSN is read only by src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. Repro steps: leave DB_OTEL_DSN empty, start svc-fv8, and send a request to port 9090. In production, traffic between svc-fv8 and svc-xjo flows over gRPC on port 9090. This record holds a gradual piece of knowledge about the cache layer of svc-fv8 and must be kept current. The svc-xjo service shares the same queue consumer, so the effect spilled over there too. Measurements showed cache layer latency dropping from 235 ms to 6 ms. For backwards compatibility DB_OTEL_DSN keeps being read under its old name until 2026-07-18. During a pairing session with Emre Arslan we wrote unit tests for the cache layer. In the next release we plan to replace E2369 with a more descriptive message. The owner of svc-xjo confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side.

## Resolution

When you see E2369, check DB_OTEL_DSN first, then the cache layer setting in src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py. Once load on the cache layer exceeds 7 requests per second, E2369 shows up. The deployment was done on 2026-07-18 by Emre Arslan with tag v2.10.8, with a rollback plan ready. The integration test for the cache layer sits next to src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py and finishes in 8 seconds. The svc-fv8 health check now fails at start-up if DB_OTEL_DSN is missing. The svc-fv8 service uses a 192 second timeout for the cache layer as of version v2.10.8. The 31-line patch in src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py stops E2369 from recurring. The config file src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through DB_OTEL_DSN. This note summarises the cache layer behaviour of the svc-fv8 service for anyone hitting the same case. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a consistent workaround.

## Follow-ups

The fix was to add a safe default for DB_OTEL_DSN and to log the E2369 condition explicitly. The first pass showed that DB_OTEL_DSN was being read differently than expected inside src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py. In the next release we plan to replace E2369 with a more descriptive message. The svc-fv8 service uses a 488 second timeout for the cache layer as of version v2.10.8. The svc-xjo service shares the same cache layer, so the effect spilled over there too. When you see E2369, check DB_OTEL_DSN first, then the cache layer setting in src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py. DB_OTEL_DSN is read only by src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. The config file src/hlmemo/storage/0001_init.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through DB_OTEL_DSN. During a pairing session with Emre Arslan we wrote unit tests for the cache layer. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a brittle workaround.

Bottom line: the cache layer of svc-fv8 is now considered unexpected. Open questions will be tracked by Emre Arslan; target date 2026-07-18. This record reflects the current state of svc-fv8 and is the first place to look when E2369 appears.

title: svc-h3j service architecture note: auth middleware
body:
## Context

The svc-h3j architecture is built around the auth middleware and talks to svc-j9q over port 8443. This document describes the components of svc-h3j and the module layout under src/hlmemo/server/app.py. The design goal for svc-h3j was to keep the auth middleware brittle and configure it through DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE.

## Environment
- DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE=8
- path: src/hlmemo/server/app.py
- error: E1121
- owner: Elif Şahin
- port: 8443
- version: v1.5.2

## Symptoms

Elif Şahin noticed brittle behaviour in the auth middleware of the svc-h3j service on 2025-10-24. The 25-line patch in src/hlmemo/server/app.py stops E1121 from recurring. For backwards compatibility DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE keeps being read under its old name until 2025-10-24. The start-up order of the auth middleware in src/hlmemo/server/app.py had changed since version v1.5.2. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-10-24; Elif Şahin finished the review. The deployment was done on 2025-10-24 by Elif Şahin with tag v1.5.2, with a rollback plan ready. The svc-h3j health check now fails at start-up if DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE is missing. We considered moving the auth middleware into svc-j9q as an alternative but decided against it. The config file src/hlmemo/server/app.py lives in version control; secrets only come in through DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE. Known limitation: svc-h3j cannot run in persistent mode without the auth middleware. When you see E1121, check DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE first, then the auth middleware setting in src/hlmemo/server/app.py.

## Analysis

This note summarises the auth middleware behaviour of the svc-h3j service for anyone hitting the same case. Repro steps: leave DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE empty, start svc-h3j, and send a request to port 8443. Once load on the auth middleware exceeds 379 requests per second, E1121 shows up. The svc-j9q service shares the same rate limiter, so the effect spilled over there too. The owner of svc-j9q confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. In production, traffic between svc-h3j and svc-j9q flows over gRPC on port 8443. The svc-h3j service uses a 77 second timeout for the auth middleware as of version v1.5.2. As a team we chose to find the root cause instead of shipping a brittle workaround. Elif Şahin proposed this in the 2025-10-24 meeting and nobody objected. On E1121 the on-call engineer verifies DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE before restarting svc-h3j. DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE is read only by src/hlmemo/server/app.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else.

## Resolution

The logs repeated code E1121 437 times, and each time the auth middleware hit its timeout. In the next release we plan to replace E1121 with a more descriptive message. Measurements showed auth middleware latency dropping from 197 ms to 25 ms. During a pairing session with Elif Şahin we wrote unit tests for the auth middleware. Because the scheduler is idempotent, every restart adds about 187 milliseconds. The fix was to add a safe default for DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE and to log the E1121 condition explicitly. The integration test for the event log sits next to src/hlmemo/server/app.py and finishes in 53 seconds. This record holds a transient piece of knowledge about the auth middleware of svc-h3j and must be kept current. This behaviour affected 17 users and went unnoticed until 2025-10-24. The first pass showed that DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE was being read differently than expected inside src/hlmemo/server/app.py. On E1121 the on-call engineer verifies DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE before restarting svc-h3j.

## Follow-ups

The owner of svc-j9q confirmed the same problem does not show up on their side. The deployment was done on 2025-10-24 by Elif Şahin with tag v1.5.2, with a rollback plan ready. Repro steps: leave DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE empty, start svc-h3j, and send a request to port 8443. We considered moving the auth middleware into svc-j9q as an alternative but decided against it. The svc-j9q service shares the same connection pool, so the effect spilled over there too. When you see E1121, check DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE first, then the auth middleware setting in src/hlmemo/server/app.py. The svc-h3j service uses a 187 second timeout for the auth middleware as of version v1.5.2. Tests went green on CI the night of 2025-10-24; Elif Şahin finished the review. DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE is read only by src/hlmemo/server/app.py; it must not be redefined anywhere else. Measurements showed auth middleware latency dropping from 410 ms to 9 ms. In production, traffic between svc-h3j and svc-j9q flows over gRPC on port 8443. For backwards compatibility DB_HTTP_POOL_SIZE keeps being read under its old name until 2025-10-24. This note summarises the auth middleware behaviour of the svc-h3j service for anyone hitting the same case. In the next release we plan to replace E1121 with a more descriptive message.

Bottom line: the auth middleware of svc-h3j is now considered transient. Open questions will be tracked by Elif Şahin; target date 2025-10-24. This record reflects the current state of svc-h3j and is the first place to look when E1121 appears.
